title: Reporting intake: Enterprise request routing, SLA lanes, and delivery visibility guide
creator: Ethan Morales
description: Create a repeatable intake and routing pattern for enterprise console/reporting requests (usage analytics, cost breakdowns, data exports, and dashboarding). The goal is to reduce turnaround variance, set clear SLAs per request class, and give customers and internal stakeholders transparent delivery visibility. This ticket captures the playbook, acceptance criteria, routing rules, example flows, and the implementation handoff to ENG/Design/Support.
acceptance_criteria: A documented routing matrix that maps request types (ad-hoc export, recurring export, new dashboard, cost breakdown customization, analytics query) to delivery lanes (self-serve, 2-week SLA, 6-week project) and required approvers.
SLA definitions and escalation steps for each lane, including expected touchpoints and status update cadence for customers.
A simple intake form template (console + CSM) and transformation rules that populate our tracking dashboard and ticket metadata automatically.
Implementation runbook for Support to set expectation and for Eng to accept work (labels, dependencies, minimal required artifacts).
A pilot with 3 enterprise customers where we measure time-to-acknowledge and time-to-deliver over a 4-week period.
Security/compliance checklist included for exports (PII/data retention/KMS requirements) and sign-off path documented.
tasks: Draft routing matrix and lane definitions
Work with Design to create intake form UI and CLI template
Align with Support & CSM on customer-facing SLA messaging
Create tracking dashboard in Console for intake queue metrics
Run pilot with 3 customers and collect metrics
Prepare handoff doc for Eng with examples and test datasets
notes: Trade-offs: highly granular lanes increase accuracy but add cognitive overhead. For MVP keep 3 lanes (Self-serve, Standard (2w), Project (6w+)).
We will prefer policy-based routing (labels + metadata) over manual assignment to avoid single-point bottlenecks.
Consider adding a paid priority lane for Dedicated/Enterprise customers in a later phase.
Exports that touch customer PII should require security gating and may be routed to Private deployments or Dedicated BAU depending on contract.
